name: coursebook
description: Open Source Introductory Systems Programming Textbook for the University of Illinois
one_liner: A free, open-source textbook that teaches systems programming in C, originally written for a university course.
buyer: No real commercial buyer — it's a free educational resource maintained by a university course team, not something built to be sold.
business_use_cases: A bootcamp or online course platform licenses/adapts the open (CC-friendly) content as the backbone of a paid 'systems programming' course.
A tutoring service uses it as free, high-quality reference material to support paid one-on-one tutoring sessions in C and systems programming.

money_ideas.idea: Package the free content into a paid, polished online course with videos and graded exercises.

steal_this: This is a public-good academic textbook, not a business. Honest take: don't build a product on it — at most, use it as free-reference-material bait to sell your own paid tutoring or a companion course.
